subject: Chinese softshell turtle
title: This Turtle Pees Through Its Mouth, and Scientists Timed It

scenes.text: This turtle pees through its mouth.
The Chinese soft-shelled turtle. In 2012, scientists in Singapore bought some at a market and watched what they did near puddles.
They dipped their heads underwater and stayed there, up to 100 minutes at a time, rinsing their mouths over and over.
Then the team measured it. Only six percent of the turtle's urea left through the kidneys. The rest came out of the mouth, up to 50 times faster than through the back end.
Why? These turtles live in brackish water. Peeing the normal way means drinking salty water to replace it. Rinsing the mouth skips that problem.
Published in the Journal of Experimental Biology. So when a turtle looks like it's drinking, check again.

description:
The Chinese soft-shelled turtle gets rid of most of its urea through its mouth, not its kidneys.
In a 2012 study in the Journal of Experimental Biology, researchers at the National University of Singapore found that turtles dipped their heads in puddles for up to 100 minutes and rinsed their mouths; only about 6 percent of the urea they produced was excreted through the kidneys, while the mouth excreted it up to 50 times faster than the cloaca. The trick lets a turtle living in brackish water avoid drinking salty water to replace lost fluid.
What is the strangest body trick you know of in an animal?
